memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: If someone has a stubborn and rebellious son who does not obey his father and mother and will not listen to them when they discipline him, his father and mother shall take hold of him and bring him to the elders at the gate of his town. They shall say to the elders, "This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious. He will not obey us. He is a profligate and a drunkard." Then all the men of his town are to stone him to death. You must purge the evil from among you. All Israel will hear of it and be afraid. - Deut 21:18-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a severe and troubling passage, and we must handle it honestly. A persistently rebellious son, one who was not merely disobedient but a hardened, profligate rebel refusing all correction, faced a grave penalty under Israel's law. We should not soften this, but we must understand it in its proper setting.

Several things help us. This was not about ordinary childhood disobedience, but about an adult son whose settled rebellion threatened the whole community. The parents could not act on their own; the matter went before the elders, requiring public confirmation. And there is no record in Scripture of this penalty ever actually being carried out, suggesting its main purpose was to underscore, in the strongest terms, how serious rebellion against God-given authority truly is. Rebellion, left unchecked, corrupts and destroys.

We live under a new covenant and do not apply such civil penalties. Yet the passage still speaks soberly about the destructiveness of hardened rebellion, and about God's grief over it. The wonderful news is that we, who have all rebelled against our Father in various ways, are met not with stones but with grace. God sent His Son to rescue rebels like us. The prodigal who returns is welcomed home with open arms (Luke 15:20). How does the seriousness of rebellion make God's welcome of returning sinners even more amazing to you?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does this passage sober you about the seriousness of rebellion?
2. Where do you see rebellion against God in your own heart?
3. How does the Father's welcome of returning sinners amaze you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You meet rebels like me with grace, not stones. Draw my wandering heart home and keep me close to You. Amen.
